# A one-sided pointed marginal need not have ordinary Gamma_d depth

This exact example blocks a geometry-only cone-partition shortcut for
adjacent integer source bases. It retains a convex body, consecutive
positive-volume fibers, and an interior point in the projecting apex
fiber. It does not assert that the apex is globally deepest or that a
common critical menu propagates from it.

Let d=2. Let D be a triangle in R^2 with centroid zero and vertices
v_0,v_1,v_2, and let lambda_i be its affine barycentric coordinates.
Put

    T=(1/10)D+(89/100)v_0,
    K_-1=2T, K_0=D, K_1=(1/100)D,
    C=conv( {-1}xK_-1 union {0}xK_0 union {1}xK_1 ).

All fibers displayed are full-dimensional. C is a full-dimensional
compact convex body. Its integer fibers are exactly these three,
because the only possible enlargement of K_0 from the two extreme
fibers is

    (K_-1+K_1)/2=(21/200)D+(89/100)v_0 subset D.

The containment follows from convexity and 21/200+89/100=199/200<1,
using zero in D. Thus no sampled fiber has been silently altered.

Project the half with integer bases z<=0 from the actual interior point
(1,0) onto base zero. In pointed coordinates x=(1-z)xi, its exact
volume density is

    f(xi)=1_D(xi)+4*1_T(xi),
    M_left=(26/25)|D|.

The factor 4 is the two-dimensional fiber Jacobian at z=-1.
For xi in T,

    lambda_0(xi)>=67/75,
    lambda_1(xi),lambda_2(xi)<=31/300.

Define

    t=(25-2 sqrt(97))/15,
    s=(1-t)/2.

In particular 0<t<67/75 and 31/300<s<1. The three CLOSED halfspaces

    H_0={lambda_0>=t}, H_1={lambda_1>=s}, H_2={lambda_2>=s}

cover D because t+2s=1. The small triangle T lies wholly in H_0 and
is disjoint from H_1,H_2. Elementary simplex slicing therefore gives

    int_(H_0) f = [(1-t)^2+1/25]|D|,
    int_(H_1) f = int_(H_2) f = [(1+t)/2]^2 |D|.

The chosen t solves 3t^2-10t+79/25=0, so these are the SAME mass Q.
Since the menu covers the support, every point of D is in a cap of
mass Q. Thus the maximum ordinary normalized depth of f is at most

    Q/M_left =25(1+t)^2/104 <4/9=Gamma_2.

The strict inequality is exact: it is equivalent to
(20-sqrt(97))^2<104, or 393<40 sqrt(97); the latter follows by squaring
positive quantities, since 154449<155200.

This disproves the proposed assertion that every one-sided pointed
marginal from an adjacent interior apex has ordinary Gamma_d depth.
It does not disprove a comparison using BOTH genuinely deepest source
menus, their common cap masses, or the full physical separator. The
body is also far from being an OC counterexample.
